text:
julie_cs: customer ping — BrightCart reporting a burst that never caught up. Per them: requests spiked from ~5rps -> ~80rps, dedicated pool only added capacity after ~4 minutes, lots of 429s and request queueing. they're pushing through us-west-2. logs attached in support ticket #BC-428 :confused:

mike_support: sorry they're seeing that. do we have repro steps or a quick curl I can run? also need org id + dedicated pool id so we can correlate autoscaler logs

julie_cs: org=brightcart, pool=dc-usw2-prod-3, region=us-west-2. quick repro curl they ran:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b", "input":"ping"}' -s -D - -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' -N
# they hammered with a simple loop to ~70-90 rps for 30s
```

ana_sre: jumping in — checking autoscaler + scheduler logs for pool dc-usw2-prod-3 now. initial glance: Autoscaler accepted scaledown/scaleup events but several new pods stayed in Pending for ~30-90s before scheduling, then InitContainers took extra ~60-90s. Not a pure kube-scheduler backlog. seeing image pull backs off in some nodes (registry backoff) and a handful of InitContainer failures: `preflight-warmup` exited 1 then restarted.

ana_sre: snippet from autoscaler:```
I0315 14:02:10 autoscaler.go:432] scale request accepted desired=12 current=4 reason=burst
I0315 14:02:12 provisioner.go:119] pod/predictor-33 pending: ImagePullBackOff (registry rate limit?)
I0315 14:03:05 autoscaler.go:459] after backoff desired=12 current=5 nextProbe=20s
```

mike_support: interesting — this is a mixed cause: autoscaler wanted to ramp but provisioning jitter (imagepull and init steps) plus root-level warmup makes the effective scale slower. customer says minReplicas=2 and they rely on warmpool to pre-attach, but warmpool heartbeats show sparse coverage.

jason_platform: I dug into warmpool telemetry for that pool — warmpool size hovered at 1-2 (they requested warmpool=3), because a recent service-account rotation caused attach failures for a subset of warmpool pods. Attach errors look like 403 from attach API until SA token refreshed (~2m window). That explains the missing pre-warmed capacity. Also saw registry pullbackoff spikes across nodes in that AZ — possibly transient quota/registry throttling.

mike_support: got it. prioritized action items? quick fixes for BrightCart to reduce customer impact now? :thinking:

jason_platform: short-term mitigations: 1) bump minReplicas to 6 for the next 24h (immediately reduces cold starts), 2) run `redwood warmpool sync --pool dc-usw2-prod-3 --force` to refill warmpool after SA rotation, 3) ask customer to stagger client ramp by 30s. Longer-term: fix SA rotation rollout to avoid attach windows and increase warmpool monitoring alerts.

julie_cs: told customer the workaround (bump minReplicas + manual warmpool sync) and asked if they can throttle ramp by 30s. they're willing to try minReplicas bump for the short term.

ana_sre: creating an ops ticket to track infra causes: OPS-9142. I'll attach autoscaler and node logs. Also flagged registry backoff telemetry to infra team. deploy-bot: kick runbook?

deploy-bot: runbook started — https://internal.redwood/runbooks/autoscale-surge-coldstart (OPENS: OPS-9142).

mike_support: great — I'm drafting a customer-facing note explaining root causes (service-account rotation left warmpool under-provisioned + transient registry backoffs -> longer init/warmup = effective scale lag). propose: action items assigned: jason=warmpool SA fix + short-term warmpool refill, ana=collect logs + escalate registry quota spikes, julie=confirm minReplicas bump and customer throttling. :thumbsup:

julie_cs: customer accepted minReplicas change, will monitor and report back in ~1hr. closing thread on escalation for now, leaving OPS ticket open until registry + SA root cause closed.

mike_support: thanks all. follow-up: consider adding a heuristic to autoscaler to account for warmpool attach failures as "unavailable warm capacity" so we don't overestimate effective headroom — filing feature request FR-233.
